- They say, that fools are always lucky, but I wouldn't believe it if I were you. Gambling is not about luck, it's about intelligence, or else you'll get swindled like a Maloq in the Galaxy Council!
loc.160.7:
You tossed <clr>5<clrEnd> cr into the blind-man's hat and he introduced you to the treasury of jail wisdom:
- Try not to lose your cellmates' respect! They do not like those who work and try to gain the goodwill of the prison authorities, but they respect those who have lots of tats and those who gable big time. They hate stoolies, and the guards would often carry out of the cell those who'd upset their cellmates in some way...
loc.160.8:
You tossed <clr>5<clrEnd> cr into the blind-man's hat and he introduced you to the treasury of jail wisdom: 
- During the weekends the real criminals like to relax, but it costs, so they extort money from other inmates, especially the outcasts. If you are not strong enough, better pay straight away. However if you join the criminal club, you too will be able to extort money from the other together with your mates. The higher your reputation is the larger your share gets.
loc.160.9:
You tossed <clr>5<clrEnd> cr into the blind-man's hat and he introduced you to the treasury of jail wisdom:
- On Sundays the prison authorities become a nice and kind lot, and would even read the petitions for reprieve written by the inmates. However in order for those to be efficient, one needs to use his brain writing his petition! Besides you need to be in good relations with the guards, or else they may simply lose your petition on their way to the warden, and so much for the release...
loc.161.0:
It occurred to you that the best way out of this situation would be passing off as a mute - he who cannot speak, cannot blabber anything out.
- Mmmmm... - you mowed and started nodding your head violently.
- What? - one of the committee members asked.
- Argh, mmmm... - you mumbled again, but this time shaking your head in negation, and even drooled form your mouth pretending to be and idiot. 
- Are you a mute? - a Peleng-woman in spectacles asked sympathetically - Poor little thing, they must be beating you here violently, force you to clean the toilets, and rob you of all your money? These guard were beating you - boom-boom - and you became and idiot?
loc.163.0:
You approached the door of the med-station when you heard some noise and loud voices coming from the inside. Stepping forward carefully, you pressed your ear against the door and tried to make out what was going on:
- Come on, you fool, no need to be shy, no one is even going to find out, y'know... - you head the voice of one of the inmates, the biggest hoodlum among all the Maloqs.
- Give it up, baby. Honest, y'know, you either give it yourself or we take it, - the second squeaking voice belonged to a Peleng, the partner of this hoodlum. 
- Leave immediately, or I will summon the guards! - the nurse's voice was shaking, but her tone was confident. Looks like she was in big trouble. And - as bad luck would have it - there was not a single guard in sight!
- You don't get it, do ya? These dudes we got'em bribed and they aren't coming back any time soon. So...

You heard a slap sound, and then the roar of the Maloq and the cracking torn fabric. What are you going to do?
loc.166.0:
You kicked the door in and broke into the room. You saw the huge Maloq wrestle with the nurse trying bring her down on the couch, and his tattooed Peleng partner bounce impatiently at his side. 

While you were watching the sight they noticed you. The Maloq rose from his victim and turning around chucked back at you:
- Say, dude, look whom we have here. Looking for something, ranger-boy? Tonight the chick serves, so to say, some very special clients at a very special tariff, so I suggest, get lost while you still can. Crystal? 
- Oh yeah, or else, the big man here, will surely tear you a couple of new nostrils... - the tattooed foot-licker spat.

You sized up the imposing frame of the hoodlum. The poor woman watched you, her eyes were pleading.
loc.166.1:
- No, homey, we are doing a good job ourselves, y'know, - the rough Maloq voice said.
- Say, big man, I'll go see who the hell is there... - with these words the Peleng jumped to the door. Flinging the door open he dragged you inside.

You saw the huge Maloq wrestle with the nurse trying bring her down on the couch, while you were watching the sight, the Peleng kicked you in the side:
- Say, big man, look whom we had there at the door.
- I swear to god, <Ranger>, - the Maloq rose from his victim, spat on the floor and chuckled with contempt: - I thought it smelled of crap around here.

You sized up the imposing frame of the hoodlum. The poor woman watched you, her eyes were pleading.
loc.168.0:
- Hey, punk, wassup with that? - the Maloq was outraged. - When exactly was it that some rotten scum started offering any deals to us?
- Who does this scum think he is, man?! - the tattooed Peleng shrieked, grabbing the nurse. 

The punch knocked you off your feet. Kicking you a couple of times, the Maloq snatched all your money from you and turned back to the girl.  
Fury got the better of you, and you bit the hoodlum's leg, not letting him go back to the nurse. He turned back to you kicking violently. The Peleng joined his partner. 

While the hoodlums were busy with you, the nurse ran to call the guards and they pulled you apart. Once the two hoodlums were taken away, the nurse straightened her coat and smiled gratefully:

- Thank you. This was very noble of you. The inmates do not like these hoodlums, and they are not going to like it when they find out that you offered them money, but I will make sure the prison authorities learn about what you did.
loc.168.1:
- Hey, punk, wassup with that? - the Maloq was outraged. - When exactly was it that some rotten scum started as much as to even talk back to us?
- Get'im, get'im, man, it makes me wanna puke when I think that a punk like this is living among us! - the tattooed Peleng shrieked, his hands all over the nurse.

The punch knocked you off your feet. Kicking you a couple of times, the Maloq turned back to the girl.  

Fury got the better of you, and you bit the hoodlum's leg, not letting him go back to the nurse. He turned back to you kicking violently. The Peleng joined his partner. loc.168.2:
- Hey, Sis, I hope you've got a couple of those bodybags somewhere in the back? - you said with a wicked grin and jumped onto the Maloq.
- Hey, punk, wassup with that? - the Maloq rushed back at you, - Let's just see about that! Hey, sweetlips, you only gonna need one bag for this scum here!

The punch knocked you off your feet. Kicking you a couple of times, the Maloq turned back to the girl.  

While the hoodlums were busy with you, the nurse ran to call the guards and they pulled you apart. Once the two hoodlums were taken away, the nurse straightened her coat and smiled gratefully:
- Thank you. This was very noble of you. The inmates are going to appreciate your courage - very few of them would have the guts to stand up to these two. And I will make sure the prison authorities learn about what you did.
jump.3.text: Sit tight, you'll have enough time to make the acquaintances
jump.5.text: Start a fight with the inmates
jump.6.text: Forget it and just stay put
jump.7.text: Kick the guard between the legs and snatch the hand-cuff key from him
jump.8.text: Smells like big trouble. Better continue foaming so that the guard does not suspect anything
jump.9.text: Kick the guard between the legs and snatch the hand-cuff key from him
jump.9.desc: Your punch didn't even visibly bother the guard. Convinced of your insincerity, he became outraged and started methodically battering you on the head with his baton. Having had his fury out on you, he let your wary head be. Soon the bus was back on the route and the now calm guard was discussing something merrily with his partner.
jump.10.text: Using the body of the guard as a shield, pull the gun out and return fire.
jump.14.text: Pretend that you are feeling better
jump.15.text: Try to snatch the gun from one of the guards
jump.16.text: Shout: "He wanted to escape and I only stopped him!"
jump.16.desc: The guard looked at you approvingly and started battering the other inmate. Most positively you just made friends with the guards, and made a large number of enemies amongst the inmates.
jump.18.text: Put down your gun and raise your hands
jump.18.desc: The guards quickly had the situation under control - batons, heavy fists, and long legs were used as a common denominator that denominated you to one big human-bruise. Soon the bus was back on the route.
jump.20.text: Run yourself, forget about the rest
jump.24.text: Submit your belongings and go to the cell
jump.25.desc: You noticed a spaceport employee, and beckoned him to come over. Showing him your gun, you took his clothes and passing off as a repair worker got to your spaceship.
jump.28.text: I am not going to give my guys in!
jump.29.text: Submit your belongings and go to the cell
jump.33.desc: You decided to get some belletristic reading - point one: it won't be so boring here then, point two: the authorities will think better of you. The interesting reading had a positive effect on your overall condition, but your reputation among the guards and other inmates went way down.
jump.39.text: Alright, sure, but what do I do with it?
jump.39.desc: - You must take good care of it, feed and constantly train it, so that the roach's speed rate are increasing all the time. And - yes - you and your pet can take part in the weekly competitions, the winner gets {250} cr. So if you manage to raise a champion out of it, you will quickly depreciate your expenses... I mean, in any event there is not much to do here save for fighting, and this way you are going to have you a small mate and something to do, so that your life is not that boring. Besides, everyone likes to watch cockroach competitions, and the owner of the champion could even go out on parole... And for now, make yourself comfortable and see what life here is about.
jump.40.text: Yes, I'd like to read something
jump.42.text: Sure, I will be your stoolie
jump.46.desc:
You headed towards the gamblers. But a huge Maloq tripped you and laughed heartily as he watched you sprawl on the floor.
- Hey, <Ranger>, you are a punk. Cards are for men.
You did not pay any attention and rubbing the bumped knee joined the gamblers.
jump.50.desc: You did some training and developed a bit of a muscle. You strength was growing.
jump.51.text: Pay {15} cr and get an "OG portion"
jump.51.desc: Today you were resting like a real man. Lots of nutritious food, meat, and all that - dirt cheap. Nonetheless the other inmates were not looking kindly upon you. You ordered yourself and OG dinner, when you weren't really an original gangsta!
jump.52.text: Space-boat anchor on your belly (350 cr)
jump.52.desc:
The Faeyan spent a whole lot of time tatting your anchor. He pierced your belly with his needles putting an intricate texture over the anchor. 
Soon the work was finished, and you proudly showed off your huge bleeding anchor to anyone who would watch. This was cool.
jump.53.desc: You did some training and developed a bit of a muscle. You strength was growing.  Although closer to the end of the training, you overdid it and dropped the barbell on your foot. It hurt but not excessively.
jump.54.desc: The skilly was as disgusting as only a skilly could be. You ate, rested, and felt a little better.
jump.55.desc:
The guard accompanying you suddenly stopped half-way down the corridor and said: 
- <Ranger>, I thought you were our stoolie. Then why don't you ever come over and report? This can really get you into some serious trouble...
He underlined his point with a heavy punch.
jump.56.text: Call the guard and tell him you wanted to speak to the chief.
jump.57.text: I want to be your informer
jump.57.desc: - Oh, really! Positively you are on the right way out of this prison. Well in that case you must come here once a week and tell me what is going on in your cell. Got it?
jump.58.desc:
You told him about everything that was going on in the cell. The chief was pleased.

- Good job, lad, I will tell the warden that ranger <Ranger> is on the way to improvement. See ya.

The guard escorted you back to your cell.
jump.59.text: I am not going to be your stoolie any longer
jump.59.desc:
The pig narrowed his slanty eyes and croaked: 
- Right, <Ranger>, think you are so smart, eh? Don't wanna be a stoolie? Wanna stay clean?!! Alright, get lost now but don't be counting on our help if anything happens to you! We'll see how tough you are...

Before you left the angered guards punched you a couple of times in the face, just for the kicks of it.
jump.60.text: Sure, I will be your stoolie
jump.60.desc: - There's a good lad. Each Sunday I am expecting you to come here and tell me everything that you know. Got it, <Ranger>? And now back to your cell.
jump.61.text: I am not going to give my boys in
jump.61.desc:
- Oh, look at Mr. Righteous here, you are not going to give your boys in, you say...
And the guards started battering you. You health has considerably worsened. Beaten and bleeding, they dragged you back to the cell, but your spirits were high - after all your reputation among other criminals has considerably risen.
jump.64.text: Naked chick on the chest (250 cr)
jump.64.desc: The Faeyan got down to work, and an hour later your chest was endorsed with a real Human babe, wind playing in her hair. The impression was that the wind was blowing her right in the face. Your cellmates marvelled at your chest, and her semi covered chest as well. A real beauty!
jump.65.desc: Today you started reading scientific literature hoping that this will make the best possible impression on the prison authorities. And that was exactly what happened. However the inmates started calling you an egghead and you quickly lost your reputation. Besides the font in these books was too small and by the end of the day your eyes started aching. But - on the brighter side - you felt you've become considerably more intelligent.
jump.66.desc: You stuck to comic books. Not really a smart reading, but you had yourself a good laugh and were feeling much better.
jump.68.desc:
A large hoodlum appeared in your way...
- Got you some rest, professor? Well, one thing you have to know, we don't like eggheads here, and we like weaklings even less.
Then followed a punch, and another one, and more... When you crawled back to your cell, you had a deep understanding, that reading was good and well, but one had to pump iron too, so that one could protect oneself.
jump.70.desc:
A large hoodlum appeared in your way...
- Got you some rest, professor? Well, one thing you have to know, we don't like eggheads here, and we like weaklings even less.
Then followed a punch... but you blocked it and returned the blow - twice as powerful. The hoodlum went down like a sack of potatoes with a broken nose.
- Lesson one, - you said monotonously. - Remember this and let the others know: the opposing force equals the initial force, which means that for each punch I will retaliate with two. I may be an egghead, but I am sure no weakling, and I will smear across the wall anyone who tries to pick on me!

After this episode, you reputation has considerably grown.
jump.73.desc: You tried to interfere, but the guards called for reinforcements. Soon they investigated into the incident, and you got a dressing-down from the prison authorities. But the inmates treated you better. Which, certainly, was not the case with guards.
jump.74.desc:
Near the cell the Don was waiting for you:
- Listen, <Ranger>, you are one smart guy and everyone respects you, y'know. Can you help me write an amnesty plea? I know how to be grateful!
You answered to his request. The Don read your writ out loud to the whole cell and everyone seemed impressed. Everyone started respecting you even more, and the Don paid you {100} cr for your help.
jump.75.desc: The evening went calm, and you managed to get some rest.
jump.81.desc: You interfered, but the guards turned out to be stronger and gave you both a good berating. Nonetheless, when the other inmates learned about what you did, their attitude to you improved considerably.
jump.82.desc: There was some really bad news in store for you. One of the guards accidentally blurted it out that you were an informer. He said he was sorry. This meant that restoring your reputation among the inmates would be extremely difficult.
jump.83.desc:
Unawares you were pacing back to your prison cell when a whole group of convicts blocked your way. The guy who looked like he was the chief around here proceeded with an explanation:

- You know, <Ranger>, you sure are one strong son of a gun, but you have to respect to our inside laws. And that cannot be tolerated.

As a result they battered you severely, trying to beat respect to insider laws into your head and other body parts.
jump.84.desc:
One of the Don's closer assistants was waiting for you near the cell.

- You worthless scum! I say your cot shall be next to the shit-hole, and I strongly advise that you do not argue.

You, sure enough, did argue, and a fight broke out. But your forces were limited and he gave you a serious beating.
jump.85.desc:
- Hey, punk. Get yourself over here - a big guy told you.

He was definitely hostile and no wonder. You reputation among the convicts was way down. Your whole body was aching for a long time after he finished battering you...
jump.86.desc:
Some rotten type approached you. 

- I know you are a stoolie. I will tell everyone, and you will answer for this, got it?
jump.87.desc:
You went back to your cell and went to bed. Suddenly you heard a siren, guards broke into the cell and started searching everyone. As a result they found a bag of heroin under your pillow. You tried to tell them it was not yours, but the authorities would not listen:
- For malignant breaching of the prison rules Convict <Ranger> will spend one week in the isolation ward.
The isolation ward was a rotten place and you lost a lot of strength and health. The trust of the authorities in you was shaken. You were completely broken and numb.
jump.88.desc:
You went back to your cell and went to bed. Suddenly you heard a siren, guards broke into the cell and started searching everyone. They did not find anything but said the cell was too dirty. When they asked who was on duty, all the inmates said:
- <Ranger> is!
- No, they are lying. I am not!
The guards believed you and punished the other convicts. But as soon as they left the inmates gave you a severe battering.
jump.89.desc:
You went back to your cell and went to bed. Suddenly you heard a siren, guards broke into the cell and started searching everyone. They did not find anything but said the cell was too dirty. When they asked who was on duty, all the inmates said:
- <Ranger> is!
 Of course you did not agree, but the guards did not believe you. You had to spend the next couple of days in the isolation ward and listen to the lectures on healthy living while in there. The authorities trust in you was shaken, as was your health..
jump.90.text: Your name - <Ranger> - on the wrist (150 cr)
jump.90.desc: The Faeyan spent a whole lot of time tracing the name "<Ranger>". He wrote it in capitals and added a ranger badge to it, so it looked real cool.
jump.93.text: Time to get yourself a new tat
jump.94.text: Flower on the right shoulder (50 cr)
jump.94.desc: The Faeyan got down to work and already one hour later your shoulder was endorsed with a huge red bud of some exotic flower, which could only be found in the Gaalian greenhouses. It smelled of nature and tenderness, so your cellmates gathered around you and stared at the bud in awe. Watching something so intensely beautiful filled their features with tenderness and sympathy.
jump.95.text: A Masonic sign all over your back (500 cr)
jump.95.desc: First the Faeyan drew a sketch and then, spent the entire day working on your back. By the end of the day your back featured something truly horrible. Everyone who saw the sign instantly started feeling respect to your persona.
jump.96.text: Broken heart on the left shoulder (100 cr)
jump.96.desc: The Faeyan got down to work and already one hour later your shoulder was endorsed with a huge red four-chamber heart with a Faeyan dropper piercing it through. It looked rather cool and your cellmates envied you..
jump.97.desc: The Faeyan was trying to refuse, failing to understand what you wanted from him, but you kept insisting. As a result your buttocks were endorsed with a proud "PISSLING" - a name the Maloqs used fore all eggheads like, say, the Gaalians.  You liked the tat very much, but your cellmates fell into two groups. The Maloqs and the Pelengs definitely liked the word, while some of the eggheads indeed took it as a personal insult. Your intellectual abilities have been assessed as very low after this story.
jump.99.text: I do not have the slightest intention of becoming a stoolie, I think I'll just go and get some rest
jump.103.desc: Unfortunately the guy who was being battered recognised you and told the entire cell in the evening what a coward you were...
jump.104.text: Oh! Today they are holding a fist-fighting championship - gotta go and see it
jump.105.text: Submit a request to take part in the tournament
jump.106.text: Submit a request to take part in the tournament
jump.106.desc:
You said you wanted to participate and were about to submit your request, when the chief guard approached you:
- So, <Ranger>, you want to take part in the tournament, well my boys just wanted to check how well you were prepared for it.
The guards dragged you to the backyard, gave you a sound beating and threw you back in your cell.
jump.109.desc: Your experience coupled with your physical abilities were at their best. Without much trouble you went into the finals and won the last match against the strongest fighter showing a beautiful and fair fighting. A reporter, who was specially invited to watch the fight, circled around the ring with his camera, yelling something about this being a sensation and an extraordinary performance. The inmates gave you a standing ovation, and the prison warden personally congratulated and awarded you and even kissed you.

jump.114.desc: You spent a wonderful day looking at the pumped up convicts beat the crap out of each other. You had great fun and your spirits were on the rise. The show culminated in the fight of two wannabe champions. Each of them has spent more than one fight in the ring, and each has made a lot of effort in order to become the best. The fight was simply amazing, and the winner was instantly set free for his merits in the ring. His opponent too was shown a lot of respect and heard a lot of nice words from the audience. All of this looked quite optimistic and you felt that next time, you'd rather participate as well.
jump.116.desc: You came into the library and started digging in the old books hoping to find something useful there. Finally you ran into an old Gaalian manuscript, or rather a copy thereof, and started browsing through the pictures, since the old tongue of this manuscript his long been forgotten by its ungrateful sons.
jump.117.desc: You liked its will for victory, and decided to make a real cockroach run champion out of it. You took it carefully and put it in a matchbox.
jump.118.text: Throw the manuscript away in disgust
jump.118.desc: The librarian saw what you did and read you a notation on the proper rules of behaviour in a library. In the end, a s a punishment, he forced you to put all the books in order on the shelves while all the other inmates left their books wherever they wanted.
jump.123.text: Today is the day of the cockroach races - go there, quick
jump.124.text: You have to put your pet on the race too. What if it wins?!!
jump.124.desc:
- An excellent species! - the head judge seemed delighted at the sight of your pet. - It will run on the fourth track. What's it called?
And then you remembered that you forgot to name your pet. 
- Err... Roach! 
- Just a roach? - the judge raised an eyebrow
- not just a roach, it's the Roach! - you said proudly.
jump.125.text: Thanks, but I think I'll skip it
jump.125.desc: - Well, whatever, make yourself at home!
jump.144.text: Go to the jail yard to train your pet there
jump.150.desc: You refused to decorate your body with pictures, but spent the entire day watching at the magnificent work of the skilful Faeyan as if mesmerised.
jump.151.text: Stake {100} cr on one of the fighters
jump.151.desc:
Since you've never participated in these competitions yourself you did not manage to assess the situation properly, and the guy whom you staked on got knocked out already in the first round... 
You lost {100} cr.
As of the rest of it, your day went just fine. You spent several hours watching big fat guys beat the crap out of each other. And in the end of the day there was an interesting match. Somebody had the guts to challenge the current champion. To everyone's surprise, the ignorant challenger turned out to be quite a strong fighter and managed to floor the champion! This has obviously made an impression on the warden and he set the winner free on parole, not wanting this tough guy hang about the prison. All of this looked quite optimistic and you felt that next time, you'd rather participate as well.
jump.152.text: Stake {100} cr on one of the fighters
jump.152.desc:
You already could call yourself an expert in fist-fighting so you were not surprised to see that the fighter you staked on won the battle. And you received {100} cr!
You were quite satisfied with both your gambling and the fights as well. Your spirits were high, and in the end of the show you watched a fight between two champions - one from the southern and the other one from the northern wing of the jail. The warden himself was present at the match, and even promised to set the winner free. The fight was totally beautiful, both of the combatants were truly worth of their champion titles! To your surprise the warden kept his word, and let the winner out on parole, and even said a couple of good words to his opponent. All of this looked quite optimistic and you felt that next time, you'd rather participate as well.
jump.153.text: Stake {100} cr on one of the fighters
jump.153.desc:
You weren't really an expert in fist-fights but you got lucky. You won {100} cr, since your fighter has become a champion.
You spent a wonderful day watching big fat guys beat the crap out of each other. Your spirits were high, and in the end of the show you watched a fight between two champions - one from the southern and the other one from the northern wing of the jail. The warden himself was present at the match, and even promised to set the winner free. The fight was totally beautiful, both of the combatants were truly worth of their champion titles! To your surprise the warden kept his word, and let the winner out on parole, and even said a couple of good words to his opponent. All of this looked quite optimistic and you felt that next time, you'd rather participate as well.
jump.154.text: Stake {100} cr on one of the fighters
jump.154.desc:
You staked your money on a very strong fighter. He almost made it to the finals but lost. The point is that your personal experience is not enough, to always stake on a winner...
Nonetheless you spent a wonderful day watching big fat guys beat the crap out of each other. And in the end of the day there was an interesting match. Somebody had the guts to challenge the current champion. To everyone's surprise, the ignorant challenger turned out to be quite a strong fighter and managed to floor the champion! This has obviously made an impression on the warden and he set the winner free on parole, not wanting this tough guy hang about the prison. All of this look quite optimistic and you felt that next time, you'd rather participate as well.
jump.165.desc: You spent the entire day cleaning the refuse in the huge jail toilet. The work was not too difficult, but it was very monotonous and dirty. You reputation dropped in the eyes of your cellmates, but the authorities seemed to be content with you.
jump.173.desc: You were lead to the hospital. Fiddling about with the sick inmates was the dullest job there could possibly be, and you were openly flunking, which did not add to your reputation neither in the eyes of the authorities, or the sick inmates.
jump.174.desc:
You spent the entire day cleaning the garbage at the jail dump site. A dull and dirty job as it was, it surely did not help your reputation among the inmates, but one has to work to be released on parole, you know. 

Closer to the end of the day you stumbled into a small and agile cockroach who ran about at the approximate speed of [p27] m/h! It's colour and size was different from the regular species, which you'd seen back in the cell - this was really one big guy. You put the cockroach into a matchbox - this guy must become a champion.
jump.175.desc: You spent the entire day unloading the heavy bags with food for the canteen. This took quite some effort and by the end of the day you were completely spent. But the authorities did appreciate your effort for what it was worth.
jump.176.desc: Together with a bunch of other inmates you went to paint the jail fence. You tried to distinguish yourself from the rest drawing some weird patterns on the fencing. Lost in the act of creation you accidentally spilled some paint on the chief guard. The inmates who stood nearby burst put laughing, the chief guard who was notorious for his rancour would surely find a way to get back at you...
jump.177.desc:
You spent the entire day working in the kitchen and stealthily eating the remains of all kinds of dishes. The catering surely helped your health and strength. Only that - the other inmates could grow envious of you...
And in the end of the day you got really lucky: you managed to steal a bottle of wine from the chef's cabinet, which you instantly sold to one of the guards for {100} cr.
jump.178.desc: You were repairing the warden's car really trying to do your best. The warden remained very content with you, but the other inmates were giving you the looks which did not promise anything good...
jump.179.desc:
You wrote an excellent essay for the warden's son, spicing it with slightly modified details of your own biography. And the prison warden was so impressed, that he even invited you to have lunch with him.
The tasty and nutritious lunch helped your overall condition, and the thoughts of being released on parole could not but please. Even the open hostility of other inmates did not spoil your mood much.
jump.182.desc:
You were given a device that emits toxic gas, and were sent about the cells to disinfect everyone and everything there. You managed just fine, until you accidentally sprayed the gas on the Don, causing the guards split their sides with laughter. 
Payback was imminent - the long time inmates weren't going to let you get away with this. Nonetheless, the authorities were quite pleased with your work.
jump.183.desc: You went to the hospital. There you took your task seriously and took good care of the sick. As a result you caught yourself a cold, your throat went sore, but the sick inmates were grateful to you for your efforts.
jump.184.desc: You spent the entire day cleaning the garbage at the jail dumpsite. A dull and dirty job as it was, it surely did not help your reputation among the inmates, but one has to work to be released on parole, you know.
jump.185.desc: You were given a device that emits toxic gas, and were sent about the cells to disinfect everyone and everything there. You managed to do so successfully, but since you weren't very experienced, you choked on the toxic vapours, affecting your health. However, the authorities were quite content with you.
jump.186.desc: You spent the entire day working in the kitchen and stealthily eating the remains of all kinds of dishes. The catering surely helped your health and strength. Only that - the other inmates could grow envious of you...
jump.187.desc:
You spent the entire day working in the kitchen and stealthily eating the remains of all kinds of dishes. The catering surely helped your health and strength. 
However the evening had a nasty surprise in store for you: having found out that a downcast was sent to work in the kitchen the inmates raised havoc and refused to eat. The warden was outraged. He tongue-lashed the guards, and demanded that they would never show such provocation ever again.
jump.188.desc:
You spent the entire day working in the kitchen and stealthily eating the remains of all kinds of dishes. The catering surely helped your health and strength. Only that - the other inmates could grow envious of you... 

Closer to the end of the day you accidentally caught a very agile cockroach that ran about with an average speed of [p27] m/h! He was much bigger than the regular species that you'd seen back in the cell. No surprise - living here in the kitchen! You put the roach into a matchbox thinking of making a champion out of it.
jump.189.text: Pay {15} cr and get an "OG portion"
jump.189.desc:
Being the boss you let yourself relax for all it was worth. The punks were bringing you food and you sharked it like there was no tomorrow, all of that was quite cheap too. Life was good!
But the guards watched you with obvious envy. No wonder their salaries were way small.
jump.193.desc:
A group of huge Maloqs met you at the entrance:

- Say, <Ranger>, wassup with that?! Punks are not wanted here!!! 

You tried to argue, but quickly shut it with somebody's fist right in your teeth. Then they locked you in the storeroom and kept you there till late in the evening.
jump.195.text: You have to put your pet on the race too. What if it wins?!!
jump.195.desc: - No, your roach is too weak yet, train it some more! - the head judge said. - We got better runners here! But sure you can gamble.
jump.211.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS JANIZARY III".
You won! With great pleasure you took the {2*[p24]} cr from the forcedly smiling bookmaker.
jump.212.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS RAKHISH RUNNER ".
You won! With great pleasure you took the {5*[p24]/2} cr from the forcedly smiling bookmaker.
jump.213.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS PENCHEKRYAK THE IDEAL".
Your pet could not offer any notable resistance to the winner, although you could see it did its best to. The race exhausted it and its speed dropped to [p27] m/h.
jump.214.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS TAMERLANE".
You lost [p24] cr! That's awful.
jump.220.text: Today is the day of the cockroach races - go there, quick
jump.226.text: I'll stake on Penchekryak the Ideal!
jump.231.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS JANIZARY III".
Your pet could not offer any notable resistance to the winner, although you could see it did its best to. The race exhausted it and its speed dropped to [p27] m/h.
jump.232.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS RAKHISH RUNNER ".
Your pet could not offer any notable resistance to the winner, although you could see it did its best to. The race exhausted it and its speed dropped to [p27] m/h.
jump.233.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS PENCHEKRYAK THE IDEAL".
You won! With great pleasure you took the {3*[p24]} cr from the forcedly smiling bookmaker.
jump.234.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS TAMERLANE".
You won! With great pleasure you took the {4*[p24]} cr from the forcedly smiling bookmaker.
jump.235.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS THE ROACH".
Your pet did it! This was the sensation of the race. The jail radio interviewed you and you became the hero of the day. You reputation in the eyes of the prison authorities grew a great lot, and the inmates were showing obvious respect as well. Besides the organisational committee of the roach races gave you an award of {250} cr. The only downside was that your pet was truly exhausted after the run...
Its speed dropped to [p27] m/h.
jump.237.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS PENCHEKRYAK THE IDEAL".
You lost [p24] cr! That's awful.
jump.238.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS RAKHISH RUNNER ".
You lost [p24] cr! That's awful.
jump.239.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS JANIZARY III".
You lost [p24] cr! That's awful.
jump.245.text: Come on, move it, boy, move it!!!
jump.246.desc: Till late in the evening the spectators were discussing the details of today's race, until the guard-on-duty told everyone to go to bed.
jump.248.text: Throw 5 cr to the blind man
jump.250.text: Throw another 5 cr to the blind man
jump.251.desc: You took a book called <clr>"The Criminal Code in the Understanding of Different Races" <clrEnd>, hoping that this would make a good impression on the prison authorities. And sure enough the authorities did like it, but other inmates started giving you the looks.
jump.252.desc: You started reading the <clr>Criminal Code<clrEnd>, hoping to make a good impression on the prison authorities. However the guards who were hostile to you reported to the warden that you were preparing a complaint against him to the prison inspection committee, which he surely did not like. However you reputation among other inmates has grown and you became smarter too.
jump.255.text: Go back to the cell, taking a spoon and a fork with you
jump.255.desc: You managed to slip <clr>a fork and a spoon<clrEnd> into your pocket and carry them out of the canteen unnoticed. Now you had to find a good way to apply these tolls!
jump.258.text: Throw another 5 cr to the blind man
jump.259.text: Throw 5 cr to the blind man
jump.264.desc:
A small Faeyan approached you.

- Sya, <Ranger>, tomorrow is my last day in prison. I need some good lad to take care of my <clr>cockroach<clrEnd>. How is that?

With these words he produced a matchbox with a tiny cockroach in it. The insect moved his antennas funnily and you couldn't but fall in love with this cute creature. It was love at first sight and you promised the Faeyan that you were going to take good care of the roach and make a real champion out of it.
jump.266.text: Buy your way out of the race for 100 cr
jump.266.desc: The Don took the money and they let you be for today. Now you could take some rest.
jump.267.desc: You told the Don to go and shove it you know. The next second the Don accompanied by several other OG's was all over you giving you a sound battering. However the other inmates started treating you with a little more respect.
jump.268.desc: You told the Don to go and shove it you know, supporting your words with a mighty uppercut. The other OG's didn't have the guts to join in, seeing what you did to the Don. You reputation grew tenfold.
jump.269.text: Let him mount you and run for all it's worth
jump.269.desc: You did your utmost and finally made it first to the finish-line. You reputation dropped a good deal, but at least nobody was beating you like they did to other "horses".
jump.270.text: Let him mount you but not run to your full capacity.
jump.270.desc: You were one of the last to make it to the finish-line. You weren't really tired but the Don was in proper fury and gave you a severe beating.
jump.272.desc: On your way back to the cell you found a banknote worth {50*([p22] div 2)} cr. You stealthily slipped it into your pocket - this definitely looked like your lucky day!
jump.273.desc:
That night the Don said half-jokingly:
- I am going to give {500} cr to him who runs a hundred times up and down the corridor. 
You decided to earn a quick cred and started running up and down the corridor, but when you were already on the {[p22]}-th lap they sounded the stand-down and the guard drove you back into the cell. Most naturally you haven't received any money, and everyone spent a long time laughing at your stupidity. However your physical shape has slightly improved.
jump.274.desc: You dared one Maloq {100} cr, that you could do 500 push-ups. This required a lot of strength but you won and got the money!
jump.275.desc: When you came back to the cell you found out that {10*[p22]} cr was missing from your locker. Tough luck!
jump.276.text: I may be a stoolie, but I never promised I was going to keep my word!
jump.276.desc: The chief guard never received the report he was expecting from you that day. This was going to cost - the chief was notorious for his rancour...
jump.281.desc:
You spent the entire day writing an amnesty plea. The result looked quite good to you. But in the evening one of the guards came over to you:
- That was a very good petition you wrote, <Ranger>! But next time make sure you write on a softer paper, that one scratched my ass real bad!
Laughing loudly the guard left. Maybe you shouldn't have spoiled the relations with the guards, since they are the ones in charge of delivering the amnesty petitions?
jump.282.desc:
You spent the entire day writing an amnesty plea. The result looked quite good to you. But in the evening one of the guards came over to you:
- That was a very good petition you wrote, <Ranger>! But next time make sure you write on a softer paper, that one scratched my ass real bad!
Laughing loudly the guard left. Maybe you shouldn't have spoiled the relations with the guards, since they are the ones in charge of delivering the amnesty petitions?
jump.283.desc:
You spent the entire day writing an amnesty plea. The result looked quite good to you. 
But the prison authorities disagreed with you on that. They were of a strong opinion that you shouldn't have used so many cusswords and calling the warden a filthy pig didn't seem like a good idea, either...
jump.284.desc: You spent the entire day writing an amnesty plea. The result looked quite good to you and the prison authorities were of the same opinion.
jump.285.desc:
You spent the entire day writing an amnesty plea. The result looked excellent to you. You were convincing the committee that this prison had the best warden there ever could be. 
The prison authorities agreed with you on that.
jump.286.desc: In the evening you had this crazy idea of starting a philosophical argument with a Gaalian OG. You couldn't convince him in anything, and it all ended with his Maloq-accomplice kicking you ass. Next time you'll be smarter!
jump.287.desc: You decided to read some romantic fiction intended for housewives. After three hours of intense reading you became a lot more stupid. The authorities appreciated your effort, but your reputation among the guards and other inmates dropped considerably.
jump.289.desc: Nonetheless you spent the rest of the day watching Sheitan-Babai win against each and every opponent. "Something's gotta be wrong with that!" - you thought to yourself.
jump.290.text: Alright - 20 cr! Give me the dice...
jump.291.text: 20 cr?! Ha!!! You're kidding me right?! 50 cr at least!
jump.291.desc:
The spectators eyed you with respect.
- 20 cr too small? - the old man asked. - You wants to rob poor old Sheitan-Babai of all he has! Alright, 50 cr it will be...
With these words he handed you the dice.
jump.297.text: Too late, time to go to bed!
jump.298.desc: - Shesh-Besh is not yer check-mate! - Sheitan-Babai said in a nagging voice and took the money. - It's a thinking game!
jump.299.desc: - Oh my! Allah forgot all about the poor old Sheitan-Babai... - the old man sighed as you put the {2*[p24]} cr into your pocket.
jump.301.desc:
- You did not play one game! - the spectators flared. - Why say that you want to play, when you are so greedy and cowardly?
Your reputation dropped slightly after this incident. Nonetheless you spent the rest of the day watching Sheitan-Babai win against each and every opponent. "Something's gotta be wrong with that!" - you thought to yourself.
jump.302.text: I reconsidered I am not going to play!
jump.302.desc:
- Why did you sit at the table in the first place then?!! - the spectators flared. - Look at this kind of a ranger, doesn't even keep his word!
You reputation dropped way down after the incident. Nonetheless you spent the whole day watching other inmates play. And by the evening you felt you were starting to get the knack of the game, you felt a bit more intelligent.
jump.303.desc:
- Let's play high! - you said. - We are grownups aren't we?!

No one argued with you and everyone threw in {500} cr
jump.304.desc:
- Let's play low! - you suggested - I want to get a better knack of the rules of the game!

Nobody argued and everyone threw in {100} cr.
jump.305.desc:
The game was complicated and multi-staged. It went on till late in the evening. You had to bargain for a widow, then follow a certain pitch and take tricks. Then the cycle repeated again. You could not get a complete understanding of the game no matter how hard you tried. Finally they started distributing the bank. Drawing something on the paper and making some calcs, the Gaalian who was in charge announced the result.
- <Ranger> won {(5*[p23]*([p22]+([p6] div 4)-([p23]-1)*(7-([p6] div 10))>0)*([p22]+([p6] div 4)-([p23]-1)*(7-([p6] div 10)))+5)/2+50*[p23]} cr.
jump.307.text: Deliver a speech advocating the rights of the jailed
jump.307.desc: Unfortunately your speech did not make much of an impression on the guards. As a result you got your portion of beating as well. The inmates started paying you little more respect, and the guards - a little less.
jump.308.text: Deliver a speech advocating the rights of the jailed
jump.308.desc: You spoke like a top-paid lawyer spicing your speech with proper legal terms. The guards decided not to mess with you and let your friend go. Your reputation in the cell has considerably grown, but the guards and the prison authorities were very displeased with the incident.
jump.309.desc: You picked a book of jokes. Not really an intellectual reading, but it improved your spirits, and in the evening you told all the best jokes to your cellmates, which they certainly liked.
jump.310.desc:
A huge Maloq, an accomplice of the Don, walked over to you:
- Today the Don will play. He will not sit at one table with a scumbag, like you! So, <Ranger>, get your ass out of here!
- I wanted to play dice... - you lied.
- Well, get your ass over there then! - the Maloq said rudely and kicked you in the general direction of Sheitan-Babai.
jump.314.desc:
You tried to start a fight, but the OG had you knocked flat on the floor in a single jab, causing the cell to awe. Without further ado he proceeded to search you, took 150 cr out of your pocket and explained:
- 100 cr is for the cause, and another 50 is a compensation to me for the inflicted moral damage!
jump.315.desc: You jabbed the OG in the face, but his friends rushed for help, and a serious fight broke out. As a result you spent a lot of strength and health, but you kept the money, and raised your reputation.
jump.316.text: Say that you do not have 100 cr, and offer a smaller sum
jump.316.desc:
Forcing you to turn out your pockets and seeing that you in fact did not have the money, the OG said:

- Alright, <Ranger>, live. Gimme what you've got! I'll let it go this time!

Taking all of your money away from you the OG proceed to racket the rest of your cellmates.
jump.317.desc:
A guard entered the cell and said:
- <Ranger>, we got a parcel for you! Follow me!
You were quite surprised but followed the guard. However instead of the promised parcel the guard took you to the chief of security, who gave you an extremely evil look and said:
- Stoolies, <Ranger>, must check in every Sunday! EACH AND EVERY SUNDAY, is that clear? So where were you today?! Never mind the explanation, I already told my boys to batter this simple truth into your shallow head!!!
At these words the guards grabbed you and started battering your head against the concrete floor which couldn't but affect your brain and general condition.
jump.318.text: Tell'em you don't have the money now
jump.318.desc:
Forcing you to turn out all of your pockets and seeing that you actually had no money on you the OG screamed:
- Are you screwing around with me, <Ranger>, are you, punk?!! Where's the freaking money?!!
And he started beating you up. Bad. You did not find the guts to put up any resistance and were beaten severely.
jump.319.desc:
A guard came into the cell and said:
- <Ranger>, we got a parcel for you! Follow me!
Surprised you followed him. And indeed, a ranger friend of yours who has by chance found himself on the planet of  <ToPlanet>, sent you a small wrapped gift - 75 cr and a pack of cigarettes. You hid the money and shared the cigarettes with your cellmates, which surely improved their attitude towards you. Your spirits have considerably improved too.
jump.324.desc: You spent the day lying on the cot and exchanging harmless jokes with your cellmates. The pastime was quite nice and you had yourself a good rest and gained some strength.
jump.326.desc: The larger part of the inmates refused to pay, and even after a severe fight you did not manage to force them to reconsider. As a result your reputation was slightly affected, and although you still managed to collect something, after the calculation your share only made {[p22]*(([p9] div 10)-6)+5} cr.
jump.327.desc: You obviously overestimated yourself. Flared at your arrogance the cellmates teamed up and gave you a sound battering. That incident surely affected your reputation...
jump.328.desc: You reputation spoke for itself, and so did the size of your muscles, that no one had the guts to mess with you. Everyone paid more than willingly. And after the split of the toll, your share made {[p22]*(([p9] div 10)-6)+5} cr!
jump.329.desc: You spent the entire day together with other criminals extorting the money from the inmates. Some of them, who were not too willing to co-operate, had to be forced to reconsider, so by the end of the evening you were completely spent. However after the toll was split your share equalled as much as {[p22]*(([p9] div 10)-6)+5} cr!
jump.331.desc: The downcast did not have the guts to argue with you. But what could you take from them? After the entire day of racketing and splitting the toll, your share totalled a mere {[p22]*(([p9] div 10)-6)+5} cr.
jump.332.desc:
The scum, for the better part, did not argue, but one of them decided to be a hero and punched you right in the face sending you down on the floor. Of course your fellow-racketeers quickly got the arrogant punk down on the ground and gave him a severe battering, but the other cellmates watched you with obvious contempt. Your jaw hurt too.
After the split, your share only made {[p22]*(([p9] div 10)-6)+5} cr.
jump.333.desc: Suddenly on the wall you spotted a cockroach that looked a little bigger than its kin. Deciding to make a champion out of it you caught it and put it in your matchbox.
jump.334.desc: You did a good work-out and built up some muscle.
jump.335.desc: You spent the entire day unloading the heavy bags with food for the canteen. This took quite some effort and by the end of the day you were completely spent. Most likely it was because of that, that you dropped one of the back down on the floor. The bag broke and the food was scattered all over the jail yard. The authorities, obviously, did not like it...
jump.336.desc: Together with a bunch of other inmates you went to paint the jail fence. You tried to distinguish yourself from the rest drawing some weird patterns on the fencing. You sure did a better job than many of the rest, but the rest obviously didn't like it, since they saw you were grovelling before the authorities.
jump.337.desc: One of the Maloqs, who just lost a game of cards, decided to let off some steam on you and punched you in the gut. It's no good being that weak!
jump.338.desc: One of the guards, who wanted to avenge you for some alleged wrongdoing, told everyone you were a stoolie. Fortunately enough, you had the brains to claim this was a lie, but the trust of your cellmates in you was still affected.
jump.339.desc: One of the guards, who wanted to avenge you for some alleged wrongdoing, told everyone you were a stoolie. Your excuses sounded lame and unconvincing, so the trust of your cellmates in you was seriously affected.
jump.340.text: Ask the guards to get you some drinks and organise a party for your cellmates, in order to improve your reputation (cost - 100 cr)
jump.340.desc: The guard answered to your request and brought you a couple of bottles of some cheap swill. You had a great time with your cellmates, but in the morning you were hungover, besides the warden was very displeased finding out about the breach of the regulations.
jump.341.text: Ask the guards to get you some drinks and organise a party for your cellmates, in order to improve your reputation (cost - 100 cr)
jump.341.desc: The friendly guard completed your request and brought you several bottles of import brandy. The cellmates were quite impressed at your coolness. You had a great party, but the warden was very displeased finding out about the breach of the regulations.
jump.342.text: Ask the guards to get you some drinks and organise a party for your cellmates, in order to improve your reputation (cost - 100 cr)
jump.342.desc: The guard answered to your request and brought you a couple of bottles of some cheap swill. You had a great time with your cellmates, but in the morning you were hungover, besides the warden was very displeased finding out about the breach of the regulations.
jump.343.text: Ask the guards to get you some drinks and organise a party for your cellmates, in order to improve your reputation (cost - 100 cr)
jump.343.desc: You waited for the guards to come back, but they never did. And judging by their drunken yells, they obviously did find a better use for your money. The entire cell was making fun of you, but, at least, maybe the guards were going to treat you better now...
jump.344.text: Ask the guards to get you some drinks and organise a party for your cellmates, in order to improve your reputation (cost - 100 cr)
jump.344.desc: The guard could not believe such an impudence, and thinking this was a provocation took the money to the prison warden with a detailed report on what you told him. The warden was very displeased, and your cellmates too were quite upset at the absence of the promised booze.
jump.345.desc: You asked the guard to call the warden and solemnly presented 500 cr to him for the needs of the prison. The warden was very pleased with you, and delivered a lengthy speech about the nobleness of your doing. As a result your reputation in the eyes of the guards has slightly risen, but the cellmates did not seem to appreciate it.
jump.346.text: I want to give you {250} cr as a token of my deep respect to you.
jump.346.desc: The warden was impressed by your deed, he even treated you to a cup of real tea. But the inmates started some very nasty rumours about you..
jump.347.desc:
The game was complicated and multi-staged. It went on till late in the evening. You had to bargain for a widow, then follow a certain pitch and take tricks. Then the cycle repeated again. You could not get a complete understanding of the game no matter how hard you tried. Finally they started distributing the bank. Drawing something on the paper and making some calcs, the Gaalian who was in charge announced the result.
- <Ranger> won {(5*[p23]*([p22]-3+([p6] div 4)-([p23]-1)*(8-([p6] div 10))>0)*([p22]-3+([p6] div 4)-([p23]-1)*(8-([p6] div 10)))+5)/2+50*[p23]} cr.

It seemed to you that you should have won more, but since you did not really know the rules that well, you decided not to start a scandal.
jump.349.desc:
A group of oversized Humans and Maloqs met you in the corner.
- You know, <Ranger>, an OG that you are we sill know that you are a weakling, and now is payback time for all the wrong you did to us!
And indeed they kept their promise and more - that was especially concerning your kidneys...
jump.351.desc: - Thank you, <Ranger>! I will never forget this! - the guard responded joyfully.
jump.352.text: Tell him you don't have that money
jump.352.desc: - You greedy son of a gun! - the guard said spitefully. - I'll get back at you!
jump.353.desc:
A group of pretty hostile guards together with the chief of security was waiting for you near the cell. The chief said:
- I see, <Ranger>, that you think you are one tough son of a gun, but we don't like tough here, and we are going to show you how much exactly we don't like them!
And indeed - the battering that they gave you was quite severe.
jump.354.desc: Fortunately enough the guy on the floor did not recognise you and the incident went without consequences.
jump.355.desc: You were given a device that emits toxic gas, and were sent about the cells to disinfect everyone and everything there. You managed to carry your task out well, and earned the approval of the authorities.
jump.356.desc: You spent the entire day unloading the heavy bags with food for the canteen. The work was very hard and you ended up hanging back on most of it, which did not go unnoticed by the prison authorities.
jump.357.desc: Together with other inmates you went over to paint the jail fence. You did not put much effort into it, but nonetheless coped with this rather easy task.
jump.358.desc:
A guard entered the cell and said:
- <Ranger>, we got a parcel for you! follow me!
You were quite surprised but followed the guard. However instead of the promised parcel the guard took you to the chief of security, who gave you an extremely evil look and said:
- <Ranger>, we brought you here in order to make a law-obedient citizen out of you, so that you repent your crimes and atone them through hard labour, sure not t play cards and dice and extort money from your cellmates. I already told my boys to batter this simple truth into your shallow head!!!
At these words the guards grabbed you and started battering your head against the concrete floor which couldn't but affect your brain and general condition.
jump.360.text: I want to pay for a professional massager (250 cr)
jump.361.desc:
The moment you sat at the table the guards broke into the cell and had everyone down on the floor..
- Time to put an end to this card plague in this prison! - the warden said. - Put all gamblers into the old isolation ward for 7 days!
A week in the isolation ward couldn't but affect your health, strength and wittiness, but your reputation in the eyes of other cellmates has grown considerably.
jump.366.desc: You paid the 100 cr and got your pet back safe and sound.
jump.367.text: Try to take the matchbox with force
jump.367.desc: One punch was enough to smear the impudent thief across the wall. You carefully picked up the matchbox that fell out of his hand, and to your great relief found your pet alive and kicking there.
jump.368.text: Try to take the matchbox with force
jump.368.desc: You bravely rushed into a fight and finally won. But, alas, your pet has been crushed mercilessly in the fight...
jump.369.desc: You punched the OG in the face and but his friends rushed forward and gave you a sound beating. However you kept your money and your reputation has grown somewhat.
jump.370.desc: You tried to stand up to him, but the OG had you down on the floor with one punch to the great amusement of everyone around you. Without further ado the OG searched you he took all of your money from your pocket and took it from you.
jump.371.desc: You dared one of the Maloqs for {100} cr, that you could do 500 push-ups. Unfortunately after {[p22]} push-ups you were already completely spent. Too bad!
jump.372.desc: Today for some reason you had this silly idea of making a sign on the wall, that read: "The Warden is a pig!" The inmates were absolutely overjoyed at your idea, but one of the guards reported to the warden, and he got quite offended...
jump.383.desc: You sat down to read a very ancient novel called "War and Peace". Unfortunately already on page 20 you were fast asleep. The authorities did not like it, but you had a good sleep and restored you strength.
jump.384.desc:
The moment you mounted the exercycle, the lights went out in the gym and a drunken Maloq voice said:

- Go back to your library, <Ranger>! We really don't like eggheads here! 

You spent a good deal of time searching for the chopper switch trying to get the power back. As a result this day was not as productive as it could be...
jump.385.desc:
Today you ran into a very exotic book called "Teach Yourself to Speak Menzol" by R. McAlister. You studied it for some three hours and finally managed to perfectly pronounce the phrase: "Aenthie makhoonkaah ist kschongha <Ranger>!" 
Your linguistic abilities have made a very good impression on everyone.
jump.386.desc: Today you took one of the volumes of the Big Galaxy Encyclopaedia and started reading about all sorts of things at random. By evening your head started aching because of all the unsystematic information, still you felt you had become much smarter. The prison authorities were pleased with you, but the other inmates thought you were an egghead.
jump.389.desc: You obviously overestimated yourself. Flared at your arrogance the cellmates teamed up and gave you a sound battering. That incident surely affected your reputation...
jump.390.desc: You obviously overestimated yourself. Flared at your arrogance the cellmates teamed up and gave you a sound battering. That incident surely affected your reputation...
jump.391.desc:
You ate very well for that money. No wonder, {100} cr - is a monthly fee of your average guard. You've recovered you strength and your spirits grew high. A champion's dinner is something only real fighters eat!
The guards' envy was truly beyond description. Just one look at your pleased gorged mug, filled their dumb heads with very cunning and mean designs.
jump.392.desc:
No one has expected such an impudence from you. You haven't been to the ring once! By ordering a "champion's dinner", you insulted the other fighters and they just couldn't eat - instead of dinner they had to use their fists a bit, teaching you a lesson. 
The guards interfered. They saved you from sure death, dragged you back to the cell, and threw you on the cot. Nonetheless the other inmates were eyeing you suspiciously not knowing what to expect next from this guy.
jump.393.text: Let's have a party! :Let's treat everyone, after all it's only {800} cr!
jump.393.desc: There was a huge bash. Everyone was having fun and eating for free. You have instantly become a respected man among all the inmates and were having fun like a true OG. The guards watched the party suspiciously and reported to the authorities. The authorities did not really appreciate this act of generosity on your side either.
jump.394.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS JANIZARY III ".
You could have won a pot of money, if you had made a stake!
jump.395.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS RAKHISH RUNNER". 
You could have won a pot of money, if you had made a stake!
jump.396.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS PENCHEKRYAK THE IDEAL".
You could have won a pot of money, if you had made a stake!
jump.397.desc:
After a short discussion the referees passed out their verdict: "THE WINNER IS TAMERLANE".
You could have won a pot of money, if you had made a stake!
jump.399.text: Complain about your hard life in prison
jump.399.desc:
- Life in here is awful! This is the worst prison for ten systems away. The guards are always drunk and they'd always batter the inmates, and the authorities couldn't care less. The warden is often abusing his power by using the inmates for his personal needs! We are forced to clean the toilets at his home, dig in his garden, and mend his personal vehicle! This is unbearable and all we inmates can hope for is a miracle! Help us!

Your conscience went numb, your head started aching terribly. What happened next remained in a blur, all you could remember were the blurred figures of the guards with electric-charge sticks, and the voice of the warden who was saying something about retaliation. When you came to, your head rang like a church-bell and the cellmates were looking at you sympathetically.
jump.400.text: Say something good about the prison
jump.400.desc:
You've got to help the warden out on this one and then, maybe, he will help you out too. That's the best choice you got. You started speaking:

- I've been here for [p1] days already. And believe me, this is the place to be. Here I started to understand that anyone who has broken the law is due to be punished.  And I have almost turned over a new leaf, all thanks to the experience of the warden here and his subordinates. Anyone who comes to this prison becomes part of the family. And once they are out the will not break the law ever again, - once you started there was no stopping you, - We also have an excellent library here, with an unbelievable selection of various books...

- Say no more, <Ranger>, you can go and have some rest, you must have had a hard day. 

As soon as you turned round the corner you let out a sigh of relief. You withstood the test. And you helped the warden quite a bit too, and he will not forget this. Only that - the other inmates are not likely to approve of your foot-licking.
jump.402.text: Hug the warden as if he were your best friend
jump.402.desc:
You put your hand around the warden's shoulder and said: 
- We are truly on friendly terms here. See, the warden is everyone's best friend, really...
Everyone's eyes became the size of dinner-plates looking at such unprecedented impudence. 
However the warden did not let you finish your tirade, landing his sizeable fist on your jaw. 

- Backslapping is not something I am going to tolerate! - the warden said - Some of the inmates you just have to be violent with. If you do not show them who is the master around here, sooner or later they will be sitting on your neck swinging their legs. Hey, guards, - her called out, - drag him to his cell. Let him think about his behaviour and remember where he is. 
The guards carried out the warden's orders with surprising preciseness, and soon you were back in your cell, waiting for the little stars to disappear and wondering why is it that the number of inmates in the cell has doubled and half of them looked like twins of the other half. You really needed some rest.
jump.404.desc:
Looks like you were in for trouble. Time to get the hell out of here you thought, and rushed down the empty corridor.  The extorters ran after you, but already 20 meters down the corridor a group of guards that was patrolling this part of the prison appeared in your way. They noticed your chasers, and somebody shouted:

- Get them, they were trying to escape! - the guards took out their batons and rushed after them.  

Phew, that was close! - you thought to yourself. Now you could go back to your cell. Although chances are you are not going to be considered a Don after that.
jump.405.desc:
You gave {500} cr to the extorters - that was certainly a blow on your budget. Well, at least they did not beat you up! Seriously, these guys could even go as far as kill you.

You sneaked back into your cell and wiped the sweat off your brow. Better not show the cellmates, that you could be scared by a bunch of pathetic hoodlums.
jump.406.desc:
The first blow landed right onto your opponent's head. You jabbed the Maloq right in the eye, he did not expect it and couldn't block the punch. The Maloq's friends jumped over you, a fight broke out, but you got lucky - because they were so blinded by their fury they were lashing out at everything and everyone within reach. You managed to crawl your way out of this mess and leave unnoticed. But the Peleng who was now occupying your place at the bottom of the pile of struggling bodies - the Maloqs will whale out on him for real.

You quickly got back to your cell.
jump.407.text: Hug the warden as if he were your best friend
jump.407.desc:
You put you hand around the warden in a friendly way and said: 
- We have very friendly relations. The warden here is like our own father. Very fair and just. This the best prison 10 systems away! The food is excellent, the guards respect the inmates and always ready to lend a helping hand, protecting the weak and keeping an eye on those who think themselves OGs, - the members of the committee were putting your speech down trying not to skip a single word and you yourself were surprised by the unexpected eloquence and kept on going: - the inmates here, we really do not feel like we are in prison. We are constantly doing something, we work, we go to the library, watch movies. And, surprisingly enough, we all feel we are becoming better persons! This prison should really serve as a role model for other penitentiary establishments...

- Thank you very much, I think we can stop here, <Ranger>. In fact I think we should really let you go wherever you were headed to!

Job well done! You hoped this rhetoric would help you in the future!
jump.408.desc:
Indeed going to the gym was a wise decision. Now the force of your punch would put a battering ram to shame! You hit the Peleng who was standing up front and did all the talking. The hit got him on the head and the poor sod went flying at about two feet's height from the floor. The Peleng goggled and screamed:
- Wendy, I can fly!!! - with that he landed right in the middle of the Maloqs scattering them around. 

You walked over to the Peleng, grabbed him by the head and said:

- Anything more you wanted to ask, suckers? 
- We'll get back on you eventually, you will learn our boss's vengeance, creep, - one of the Maloqs whispered. Big mistake. He shouldn't have said that. Had he kept it shut, you probably wouldn't have noticed him in the thick shadows. You flung your foot in the general direction of the sound and heard something crack under your heel.

Not taking another look back at them you proudly proceeded to your cell.
jump.415.text: Treat the tired guards at the entrance - {100} cr!
jump.415.desc:
- This is a token of gratitude to our honourable officers on guard of the prison's peace, - you said half-mockingly, - I would like to express my gratitude by treating you to a small feast! 

With this said dishes started appearing on the guards' two tables, these guys would never have been able to afford a feast like that with their salaries. Without much ado, the three guards hawked down upon the food, that the cooks had brought - fresh bread, juicy meat, hot appetisers, and even some wine! The guards are not supposed to drink when on you duty, but hell - a free lunch is a free lunch. From this moment on the guards would be treating you well! 

Unfortunately though, other inmates did not appreciate your doing. Nor did the prison authorities, so chances were you would not be able to do this again.
jump.416.desc: <clr>Power attracts power<clrEnd> - this was the rule which you decided to use when working out. The bigger the muscle mass, the more trouble you will be able to unleash upon the sorry heads of your ill-wishers. You completed an exhausting set of weight-lifting exercises and push-ups. Whoever said sports helped build up strength? Sports helped build up one hell of a strength!
jump.417.text: No we are not going to shake anyone down. Let them lay a table for me from the parcels that they'd received from their homes.
jump.417.desc:
The inmates were glad to get away from it that easily, and quickly laid the table for you. But the other original gangsters did not approve of that decision, thinking that you simply dodged you responsibilities on racketing other inmates.

Hurry up there's an exuberant lunch waiting for you in the canteen!
jump.419.text: No we are not going to shake anyone down. Let them lay a table for me from the parcels that they'd received from their homes.
jump.419.desc:
The best way for a Don to be is use the policy of peaceful authority. Do not extort money too often, and just ask the other inmates nicely to feed you. Eat your cake and have it, you know. The inmates told you there was an excellent lunch waiting for you in the canteen, comprised of dishes from all over the Galaxy.

- Come to the canteen, boss, - one of your accomplices addressed you - everything is ready for you there.
jump.421.text: Try the treats from the inmates
jump.421.desc:
Indeed the lunch was swell. Back on the freeside this would have probably been enough to organise a wedding party. Roasted meat of milk oinkers, seafood delicacies, soft drinks from all over the Galaxy, you name it. 

The guards saw the inmates give you all that food for free and reported to the warden. He marked you file up as that of  a potential extorter.

The feast really helped you recover your strength!
jump.428.text: I need to be fixed a little
jump.431.text: Back on the freeside the doctor prescribed me to take 40% spirit solution from  all illnesses
jump.432.text: Do you have any plans for tonight?
jump.433.text: I think I will go back to the cell.
jump.435.text: No, that's a bit too steep
jump.437.text: Treat your cellmate to the spirit
jump.437.desc:
You got the spirit and sat down together with your cellmates at a separate table in the far corner. Man that was one heck of a party! As a result you understood one simple truth - the stronger the spirit the stronger the bonds of friendship between those drinking it. Your reputation among the cellmates has skyrocketed.

But the guards and the prison authorities were not happy about what you'd done.
jump.476.desc: You let the Human go instead of you, he shook you hand, shoved all his money into it and rushed down the tunnel. Suddenly you heard steps in the corridor. A round! With one mighty blow you crashed down the ceiling of the tunnel. Judging by the sound that followed the larger part of the sap has collapsed, so now the guards will not be able to find anything here.
jump.478.text: I need to be fixed a little
jump.481.text: Go to the hall of the cunning Pelengs
jump.482.text: Go see the amateur's night at the Humans'
jump.484.text: Visit the Gaalian feast of the spirit
