jump.510.desc:
You remembered a famous gangsta-rap song, which your cellmates liked to sing:

- Been spending most our lives, in the heaven of gangsta's paradise! 

The hall joined along in the chorus, this was a very good move - you touched a soft spot with this one here, and the inmates rewarded you with a standing ovation. 

But the authorities did not approve of your artistic talent...
jump.511.desc: As soon as you started singing the hall started yawning and shooed you off the stage, upstaging your singing with their shouts. In shame you went away.
jump.512.desc: You had this excellent merry song just at the tip of your tongue. You sang it twice, cheering up the inmates and even the guards - indeed laughter extends life... "And term too!" - the warden though as he dropped in to see what the inmates were doing in the Human hall. He really did not agree with the concept of jail as a merry place.
jump.513.desc: You started singing the reggae but since you did not know the words, you simply sang about what you saw around you. The inmates, the guards, the hard life without a breath of fresh air. The audience liked it and stomped their feet and shook their heads to the beat of your song. But the guards, who looked more like they were into hardcore, did not appreciate your performance, and your reputation in their eyes has dropped.
jump.518.text: Throw 5 cr to the blind man
jump.519.text: Throw another 5 cr to the blind man
jump.527.desc: You did not put a lot of effort in your work looking mostly at your feet and thinking about what you could do. Suddenly you spotted a stick with little holes in it on the ground. You picked it up and saw it was a little pipe. You blew it not really expecting to get much out of the thing, but the music was surprisingly beautiful. You stopped and slipped it into your pocket, away from the unwanted eyes.
jump.532.desc: On your way back to the cell you saw a Maloq who was fumbling about with a <clr>cube puzzle<clrEnd>. You stopped, but he paid not attention all wrapped up in an exhausting thinking process. After five minutes of futile attempts, he threw the cube on the floor and went away mumbling something under his breath. You <clr>picked up the puzzle<clrEnd>.
jump.541.desc:
You broke away from the cell and ran to the warden. He was in his office, busy with piles of paper, and did not want to see anyone, but you insisted. You told him that your Peleng cellmate has dug out a whole tunnel to run away from prison. The warden and a whole platoon of guards broke into the cell right in time to find the creep make his leave through the tunnel. 

The warden shook your hand and personally thanked you for co-operation. The attitude of other inmates towards you has gone down.
They backfilled the tunnel ruining your hopes to run away.
jump.548.desc: - Thank you, <Ranger>! You helped me big time here. I will not forget this. Here, take this {300} cr, I think this is a decent payment for you helping me to escape, - the Peleng said and moved into the sap. He started screwing himself through the ground, not forgetting to crumble the ceiling behind him, covering the tracks. Now you will have to dig it all again.
jump.549.text: No need to get so worked up about this! Run, no problem!
jump.549.desc:
- Oh, <Ranger>, looks like you are a cool guy after all. Thanks, - the Maloq grabbed your hand and squeezed it painfully. - Here, take this {140} cr, I am sure it will help you here. In fact I never really expected you to be that quick! From this moment on you are like a brother to me, I mean, I was to spend another couple of years in this hole! I will try to get you out of here. Bye! 
The Maloq squeezed himself through the narrow tunnel and started to crawl cursing loudly. Gradually the sound died out. Couple of minutes later the insecure tunnel collapsed, and you kept wondering whether the Maloq has actually made it.
jump.561.desc:
You told the Human to pack for the road, and excusing yourself for a minute, rushed back to the warden. The guard at his office asked you what you wanted and led you inside. The imperious warden stood facing the window, his back to the door, and massaged his hands - must have been teaching the negligent convicts with his signature baton again. The guard quickly reported what had happened. 
A SWAT team was sent to your cell. They crumbled the tunnel, handcuffed the human and took him away unconscious.

Now the warden respects you, and the guards are trusting you a little more, but it looks like the inmates are suspecting something.
jump.562.desc:
Without a word you left the cell. Unnoticed you carefully sneaked through to the warden's office and reported that there was a Maloq locked up in your cell doing something suspicious. A group of huge guards was summoned, and they caught the Maloq right at the moment when he was trying to squeeze himself into the narrow tunnel. It took the guards just a couple of minutes to backfill the tunnel.

The Maloq was given two more years in control unit. 
The warden thanked you heartily, and the guards started trusting you more.
But the inmates were treating you suspiciously, now that the knew about the set up.
jump.564.desc:
- Yes - what? - the warden asked.
- I mean, "yes", it's all these guards - they are beating me up everyday, and on weekends and holidays, the beat me twice a day! The guards in this prison are real hoodlums, and we - the poor convicts - fear them more than the Dominators... 
- Why did you loose your ability to speak and become a mute? - one of  the committee members asked. Unfortunately it was too late...:
- Don't you see that this convict is simply making fools out of us? - the warden boomed angrily approaching you - his baton ready. - It appears, <Ranger>, that it is about time you got this nonsense out of your head. Who knows - maybe then you will regain your ability to speak - one nail drives out the other, or so they say...
- MMMMMM, - you shook your head in fear, but the warden has already given a sign to the guards and they started battering you. They made sure they got your head first, carefully following the warden's instructions on that. At last you pled for mercy.
- See, - the warden addressed the inspection committee, - thanks to the efforts of our massagers, this convict has stopped being a mute. And you know, I could go for hours on end about the miracles of our labour therapy...

But the miracles of labour therapy fell out on you, because you passed out. When you came to you already were back in your cell.
jump.566.desc:
- You mean to say, that the guards have nothing to do with this? - she wouldn't let you go.
- Uhm, - you nodded affirmatively and tried to explain in sign language that the guards treated you well. 

- See, - the warden jumped at the occasion, - our prison is open for everyone, be it a cripple or a popular politician. We make no difference here, we welcome everyone with equal hospitality and try to take care of our subjects. And here is a perfect example - when convict <Ranger> first got here he used to have fits of fury, suffered from flatulence and other illnesses, but constant care and the warm and friendly atmosphere of these walls helped him overcome his disease, and I am positive that when he leaves us he will become a rightful member of society. And I can even promise this - it's going to happen much sooner than he himself is expecting! - with this said the warden led the committee over to the prison hospital.

Prostrated you went back to your cell. It did seem to you though that the warden was smiling at you rather sincerely, which could not be said about your cellmates, who looked hostile.
jump.567.desc:
- So, you mean to say that the guards are beating you up violently? - she would not let it go.
- Mhm, - you nodded again and tried to explain in sign-language that one should go look for such beasts as these morally depraved scumbags. The phrase looked quite awkward to the point of being insulting in your performance, but they did understand you, and the warden was the first person to understand you.
- Do not pay attention, - he smiled peacefully. - This is our local sort of God's fool, he is totally harmless, although his brain is probably smaller than that of a demented penchekryak. Despite all the love and care that we show for him, he would sell his father's soul for a gleaming hair-pin, and he makes nasty things for everyone. You can't blame him though, a police patrol found this sob on an asteroid where he was raised by the wild kwadakhis. When we found him, he ate moss and peed in his pants. Even asylums and psychiatric clinics refused to take him, and I felt sorry for the guy and agreed to undertake the care over him. 

One of the guards scowled, and the Peleng female inspector patted you on the head and gave you a <clr>cube puzzle<clrEnd>. Prostrated you went back to your cell clenching on to the gift of the tender-hearted Peleng female.
jump.569.desc:
- No - what? - the warden asked.
- I mean "no", I had been a mute already before I got here. And the local OG's are constantly beating me up, and it made a fool out of me. Had it not been for the guards, they would have had me killed altogether...
- I always thought a "mute" was somebody who cannot speak, - one of the guests suggested thoughtfully.
- Yes, that's it I can't spe... - it was only now that you understood WHAT was actually happening.
- Don't you see that this convict is simply making fools out of us? - the warden interjected. He didn't like your trick, and pushing you away in contempt he led the committee to the prison hospital. But the guards on the other hand liked your sense of humour and were pleased at the kind words you said about them. When you came back to your cell the inmates eyed you with disgust.
jump.570.desc:
- So, you mean to say that the guards are beating you up violently? - she would not let it go.
- Mhm, - you nodded again and tried to explain in sign-language that one should go look for such beasts as these morally depraved scumbags. The phrase looked quite awkward to the point of being insulting in your performance, but they did understand you, and the warden was the first person to understand you.

Even asylums and psychiatric clinics refused to take him, and I felt sorry for the guy and agreed to undertake the care over him. 

One of the guards scowled, and the Peleng female inspector patted you on the head and gave you a candy, which you ate at once. Prostrated you went back to your cell.
jump.573.text: Quietly walk away, before they noticed you.
jump.573.desc: "Looks like today the medical station is closed today ", - you thought to yourself on the way back to the cell.
jump.574.text: Knock and ask any help was needed
jump.575.text: Take a deep breath and break in
jump.576.text: Sorry I was just passing by (run away)
jump.576.desc:
Deciding not to mess with these hoodlums you, you turned away and rushed off like there was no tomorrow. Stopping round the corner to catch your breath you listened. Suddenly the door of the station blasted open and the screaming Maloq burst out, his hands clutching the place which one usually sits on. You saw blood drip between his fingers, and a scalpel handle protruding between his hands. A squeaking Peleng who had his hands covering his face followed his grand entrance. Judging by the patches of skin that showed through he has just been treated to a glass of highly concentrated acid.

Now that the hoodlums were no longer a threat, you went back to the medical station. The nurse stood in the corner clenching a scalpel, one of her sleeves was torn. 
- Pathetic coward! - she spat in your face. - I've seen you run off with your tail between your legs like a filthy jackal... I will tell everyone what kind of a scumbag you are, leaving a helpless woman in the hands of these hoodlums! Out of my sight!!!

"Helpless - yeah, right", - you though to yourself on the way back to the cell.
jump.578.text: Alright, you scumbags, prepare to die! (attack them)
jump.578.desc:
- Hey, Sis, I hope you got a couple of them bodybags somewhere in the back? - you said with a wicked grin and jumped onto the Maloq.
- Hey, punk, wassup with that? - the Maloq rushed back at you, - Let's just see about that!  His sizeable fist shot forward... But you surely had not been wasting your time in the gym! 

Ducking his blow with ease, you punched him back in the gut - hard to miss such a large target - as he bent forward you caught his chin on your knee. The Peleng who tried to interfere you took out with one single blow. While you were busy with them the nurse ran off to call for help and the guards dragged away the bodies, that tried to show signs of life. 

Once the hoodlums were carried away, the nurse straightened her coat and smiled thankfully:
- Thank you. This was very noble of you. Most of the inmates do not like these hoodlums, and they will surely appreciate what you did, and I will make sure that the authorities learn about what happened too. Oh, and also I could give you some <clr>spirit<clrEnd> for <clr>free<clrEnd> or else help you <clr>fix your health<clrEnd>.
jump.579.text: I suggest that we settle this peacefully - I am going to give you {500} cr, and you leave the girl alone
jump.579.desc:
- Err, dude, you actually like mean it? - the Maloq scratched the back of his head.
- Hey, man, who does this punk think he is - the tatted Peleng shrieked his hands all over the nurse.

You took out the money and waved the bundle in front of the hoodlums' noses.
- <clr>Five-Hund-red<clrEnd>, - you articulated again. The eyes of the Maloq followed the money intensely. Finally he could not take it anymore and snatched the creds away form you.
- Hey, bro, let's get the heck out of here. Tonight we are going to have some quiet fun, courtesy of Mr. <Ranger> here, - he said peeling his partner off the girl.

When the hoodlums left the nurse straitened her coat and smiled thankfully:

- Thank you. This was very noble of you. The inmates do not like these hoodlums, and they are not going to like it when they find out that you offered them money, but I will make sure the prison authorities learn about what you did. Oh, and also I could give you some <clr>spirit<clrEnd> for <clr>free<clrEnd> or else help you <clr>fix your health<clrEnd>.

- Alright-alright, dude, I mean you are an OG, and I am not going to cross you. Let's settle on {250} creds.
You gave him the money.

jump.582.text: Hey, yo! Isn't it time for you girls to go home? Yeah, you...
jump.582.desc:
- Hey, punk, wassup with that? - the Maloq was outraged. - When exactly was it that some rotten scum started as much as to even talk back to us?
- Get'im, get'im, man, it makes me wanna puke when I think that a punk like this is living among us! - the tattooed Peleng shrieked, his hands all over the nurse.

His sizeable fist shot forward... But you surely had not been wasting your time in the gym! Ducking his blow with ease, you punched him back in the gut - hard to miss such a large target - as he bent forward you caught his chin on your knee. The Peleng who tried to interfere you took out with one single blow.

While you were busy with them the nurse ran off to call for help and the guards dragged away the bodies, that tried to show signs of life. Once the hoodlums were carried away, the nurse straightened her coat and smiled thankfully:
- Thank you. This was very noble of you. Most of the inmates do not like these hoodlums, and they will surely appreciate what you did, and I will make sure that the authorities learn about what happened too. Oh, and also I could give you some <clr>spirit<clrEnd> for <clr>free<clrEnd> or else help you <clr>fix your health<clrEnd>.
jump.584.text: I suggest that we settle this peacefully - I am going to give you {500} cr, and you leave the girl alone
jump.584.desc:
- Hey, punk, wassup with that? - the Maloq was outraged. - When exactly was it that some rotten scum started offering any deals to us?
- Who does this scum think he is, man?! - the tattooed Peleng shrieked, grabbing the nurse. 

The punch knocked you off your feet. Kicking you a couple of times, the Maloq snatched all your money from you and turned back to the girl. Fury got the better of you, and you bit the hoodlum's leg, not letting him go back to the nurse. He turned back to you kicking violently, but you already recovered from the initial shock and show him what you were good for. This guy was strong - it was not for nothing that even the OG's were afraid of him, but you weren't that bad a shot either. You took out the Peleng - who had the idiocy of trying to join in - with one jab. And five minutes later you took all your money back plus {100} cr more from the unconscious Maloq.

jump.589.text: I think I could use some spirit...
jump.591.text: Yes, I don't really feel well - so I could use some professional assistance
jump.591.desc:
- So I noticed, - she smiled. - Looks like conventional methods are not going to help here, but don't you worry, hero.

With these words she produced a syringe filled with some reddish liquid.
- This is "Regenerine-X", a substance that increases the speed of tissue regeneration by dozens of times. Used by the airborne, to recover from their wounds quicker. 

And indeed, one shot of this thing instantly fixed you.
jump.594.desc:
The moment you sat at the table the guards broke into the cell and had everyone down on the floor..
- Time to put an end to this card plague in this prison! - the warden said. - Put all gamblers into the old isolation ward for 7 days!
A week in the isolation ward couldn't but affect your health, strength and wittiness, but your reputation in the eyes of other cellmates has grown considerably.
jump.595.desc:
The game was complicated and multi-staged. It went on till late in the evening. You had to bargain for a widow, then follow a certain pitch and take tricks. Then the cycle repeated again. You could not get a complete understanding of the game no matter how hard you tried. Finally they started distributing the bank. Drawing something on the paper and making some calcs, the Gaalian who was in charge announced the result.

- <Ranger> won {100+5*[p22]} cr. Hey, you really play with class, <Ranger>! Maybe next time we can play high?

jump.599.text: I wanted to ask you for a tape-recorder - I am going to need it on the mission
jump.599.desc:
- Ha, that's an excellent idea, <Ranger>! - the chief of security exclaimed. - How come I did not think of it myself?! 

With these words the chief of security took a small tape recorder from his desk and gave it to you. 

- And now, <Ranger>, since you are here, tell me what's going on in your cell...

You had no other choice but to tell the guard about everything that was going on in your cell. He was pleased with you and promised to help with releasing you on parole. Finally he let you go, and one of the guards escorted you back to the cell.
jump.601.desc: You stopped by the toilet and found a <clr>pipe<clrEnd> lying on the floor- apparently somebody had left it there by chance. You examined the instrument and seeing that it wasn't broken slipped it in your pocket. Now you could really show something at the amateur's nights!
jump.603.text: Go back to the cell, taking a spoon and a fork with you
jump.603.desc: You slipped the fork and spoon into your pocket and tried to sneak out of the canteen. But it was not that easy. The guard a the door stopped you and prevented you from stealing prison property. He gave you a kick, took the fork and spoon away from you, and reported the incident to the prison authorities, which couldn't but affect their opinion about you.
param.0.crit:
В камеру зашел охранник.
- Заключенный <Ranger>! Вы отбыли свой срок и согласно решению верховного суда планеты <ToPlanet>, будете немедленно освобождены. Прошу пройти за мной на выход, где вы получите назад свои личные вещи. Сам начальник тюрьмы хочет попрощаться с вами.
...
Через несколько часов вы уже вышли из тюрьмы, получив свои вещи назад. Ваш любимый корабль был опечатан чиновниками и вы, сорвав эти пломбы, радостно плюхнулись в свое пилотское кресло.
param.2.crit:
A guard entered your cell.

- Convict <Ranger>! You have served your term, and according to the decision of planet <ToPlanet>'s supreme court, shall be released immediately. Please follow me to the exit where you will get back your belongings. The warden himself wants to say good bye to you, free citizen of the Galaxy.

Several hours later you already left the prison, having received back your personal belongings. You favourite ship was sealed by the bailiffs, and - ripping the seals off - you joyfully jumped into your pilot seat.
param.3.crit:
A sharp jolt of pain jerked right through you, you felt the taste of blood in your mouth. You sank down to the floor and everything went dark before your eyes. Somebody screamed, and you saw a blur of shadows run in front of you... 

Already in hospital they sent many electrical jolts through your body trying to get the heart beat again, but, alas, no modern medicine or cusswords could bring you back...

You were buried at the prison cemetery. The warden himself delivered a touching speech, expressing his grief at the loss of a person like this and even cancelled the entire work for today.

The open hostility of your cellmates came to the point of a rebellion:
- For how long this scum <Ranger> will be polluting the air of our cell? Why do we have to tolerate the presence of this bastard who is a disgrace to the name of all honest criminals? - a one-eyed Peleng, the right hand of the Don shrieked, banging his chest with all his four fists. The chest of the "honest criminal" was proudly decorated with a tat, which read "motherland for sale, cheap". A huge Maloq who was the Don's left hand rose from the cot:
- Punks like that must be slashed in the toilet! - he roared and meaningfully drew his palm across his throat. The words were taken as direct instruction, two bulls twisted your hands behind your back and the third one pushed your head down the toilet-bowl and held it there until you suffocated.

A worthy end for a space ranger!!!
